title: Lord of Vengeance Covenant for Eternal Life or Death

sense.text:
“Declaring the end from the beginning”: declaring the future from the past. “And from ancient times the things that are not yet done”: the ancient times are the past, and the things that are not yet done are the future. There is a past and there is a future, and we are in the very present. In this gospel truth the Bishops and the Deacons have been bringing clarity to the word of God of the past, showing where we are now, and prophesying the word of God to show us the future. But all of it is of the Most High God, because he declared the end, the future, and he spoke about it even in the very beginning.

“Saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.” So who is going to stop that? Is Esau going to stop that? Is Moab going to stop that? Are we going to stop that? Are you? No, you ain’t going to stop nothing. The Most High said it; he is declaring it.

precepts.why:
Ezra asks, trying to get understanding: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” The end of the first, and the future of it that follows.

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” Then: “For Esau is the end of the world.” There it is. God already declared it: Esau, your so-called white man, your so-called Caucasian, he and his people are the end of the world. “And Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth”: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the 12 tribes of the children of Israel, are the future, the beginning of the world that follows. God declared it, whether you answer it or not, and it’s right anyway.

The Most High means business; he is not playing. He declared this from the very beginning, in the Book of Genesis, when Esau and Jacob come on the scene: God was declaring then, from the beginning, what was going to happen in the future.

“The grass withereth, the flower fadeth”. Look outside today and you notice the season has changed. The grass is not growing as fast as it used to, you start seeing patches, the leaves falling off the tree, the flowers that just bloomed falling to the ground the next day, the tree limbs getting crackly and brittle. We see that happen periodically throughout the year, in the season, “because the spirit of the Lord bloweth upon it”.

“But the word of our God shall stand for ever.” The grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God is going to stand forever, just as his counsel shall stand. So it’s high time for you to wake up out of your sleep: this word of God is going to be manifested with or without us, with or without you.

sense.text:
This is the title of the class: the Lord of Vengeance, covenant for eternal life or death. “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

First it mentions the salvation of the righteous, and that is what is most important right now. Our main focus as the men of God, as the children of God, should be the salvation of the righteous. That’s why we go out into the hedges and highways, and why the prophets of God are out there risking their lives for the nation of Israel, not just here in America, Babylon the great, but now going out to the four corners of the earth.

So deal with the salvation of the righteous first and don’t worry about the destruction of the enemy, because the Most High already declared it; that comes at the very end, and we’ll go out with a bang on that one and celebrate together. Our work right now is getting our people right, getting their minds right, because salvation is getting ready to come, and when it comes it can be either eternal life or death. We are just now beginning.

We know we are in the land of our captivity, and we know who our enemies are, but many out there don’t believe it and don’t know it. So we have a heavy job and much work to do. As the men of God, and likewise you women, we are held accountable: much is given and much is required. It isn’t just on me; it’s on you too. I have to step my game up, and so do y’all.

“If they sin against thee”: this is the 12 tribes of the children of Israel, which they did. “For there is no man that sinneth not”. “And thou be angry with them”: God has been very angry with the 12 tribes of the children of Israel. “And deliver them to the enemy”: that happened. “So that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”: far and near.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”: if they shall remember. “And repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives”. That’s why we were up in prayers this morning, making supplication in the land where we were carried captive, and I pray y’all have been doing the same thing. Our Bishop always tells us to study, pray and apply. We have to tighten up; I’m out there with you.

“Saying, We have sinned”: if you don’t say nothing else, say, Lord, we have sinned. “And have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”. Is that not true? You can see it on TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, anywhere you look, and on TV: everything is perverted wickedness. All these Tyler Perry movies coming out are just insulting us as black folks here in America, Babylon the great, and most of the actors on his shows are homosexuals or lesbians; that’s what it’s all about. But it isn’t only Tyler Perry: all the 12 tribes of the children of Israel, going back in history, have done perversely and sinned, and that’s why we have been judged today in the land of our captivity.

But if we bethink ourselves, correct ourselves, bring to mind what we have done and repent of it, then there can be salvation; there can be eternal life for us.

Young men, pay close attention, because this is vital: being in this gospel truth is one of the most important choices you can make in your life. You are going to have challenges. Never give up, never give in, even if you have to lose your life. Do you want to go through this again, what our people went through in the past? Do you want your kids and your grandkids to go through it again? You are the ones the Most High is raising up in these last days like never before to prophesy, the ones who will help bring this kingdom down. You have purpose. Don’t let them make you a basketball player, a football player, running track, boxing, singing and dancing, cooning for your oppressor; it won’t get you anywhere. Look what happened to Kanye, or Ye, and these entertainers: used up and then destroyed. Look at Ryan Garcia, the boxer: now they are saying he’s going crazy, because he realized it is all the enemy, it’s all a trick bag. He has been out to some crazy island where they sacrifice people and seen those rituals, and now he’s telling people this is an evil and wicked place and we need to come out of it. Sisters, y’all have a place in this too.

precepts.why:
Again: we bethink ourselves in the land where we were carried captive, and repent and make supplication. Supplication means to cry out to the Most High God and acknowledge that we have sinned and done perversely and committed wickedness. All have sinned and fallen short of the glory.

“I will go and return to my place”: the Most High God said, I’m going to go and return to my place, “till they acknowledge their offence”. The Most High wants to dwell in the midst of his people, in the midst of the righteous, the repentant people, but he can’t do so right now until we acknowledge our offense.

That is what we just read in First Kings 8: acknowledging our offense, not as individuals but as a nation of people. I played a part in it just like all of y’all did. We have to bethink ourselves and acknowledge our offense, so that the Most High will come back and dwell in the midst of us.

sense.text:
“And it came to pass in process of time”: going back in the past. “That the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage”. They were tired by reason of bondage. When are we going to do the same thing? When are we going to sigh by reason of bondage, and be sick and tired of being sick and tired? It is going to take some affliction; that’s what is going to bring it out of us.

“And they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.” That’s why leadership says study, pray and apply, and bring forth supplication: they cried, and their cry came up unto God. Some of you are comfortable here; some of you like this. I’m sick of it. When are you going to be sick of this bondage?

“And God heard their groaning”. If the Most High heard them then, do you think he won’t hear us now? He heard their groaning, their cries, their sighs.

“And God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.” Say it one more time: with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. We could make a song out of that, because he made a covenant with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob.

“And God looked upon the children of Israel”. Remember: I will go and return to my place till they acknowledge their offense. Here he looked upon Israel.

“And God had respect unto them.” They say God is no respecter of persons. Yes he is: he has respect unto them, the children of Israel.

precepts.why:
“My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips.” The Most High is not changing, not for you or for me. He will not break his covenant nor alter the things that come out of his lips. He declared the end from the beginning, and it ain’t going to change.

“Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David.” The Most High God said himself, I have sworn by my holiness and I will not lie. So God does not lie.

“His seed shall endure for ever”: whether you are with us or not, his seed is going to endure forever. “And his throne as the sun before me.” The sun hasn’t been blotted out; it has been going on from the beginning, when he said let there be light.

“It shall be established for ever as the moon”: we just had a new moon, the feast of the memorial of blowing of trumpets, and it is going to continue on; it’s not going to stop. “And as a faithful witness in heaven.” Just as God is faithful, the sun and the moon are a faithful witness in heaven. Who created the sun and who created the moon? If you rely on and believe what man tells you, you are lost. There’s got to be a God that can create the moon and the sun; tell me there ain’t no God and what’s wrong with you? We say you … are crazy.

sense.text:
“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you”. We have to go through these things, and there is a reason. Fire will destroy, but God controls fire to the point that fire can purge and cleanse. That is what he is going to have to do here in America, Babylon the great: destroy everything here, and cleanse it. It isn’t only destroying, it’s purifying. When you heat gold in the fire it removes the dross off the top, and you get the pureness of it. So fire can be used for destruction as well as be profitable, but you know not to play with it; you have to take it seriously. So the Most High is letting us know we have to start taking this thing seriously.

Don’t think it strange when stuff happens. You might be going good for a while, but sooner or later something will come your way and you will be tried on these very words you have been preaching and teaching out in the streets, the hedges and highways. “As though some strange thing happened unto you”: man, what happened to you? You know what it is: being tried.

“But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings”. That’s hard, because the spirit and the flesh are battling each other, but the Bible says rejoice that you are partakers of the sufferings, “that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.”

“If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you”. Then you know the spirit of God rests upon you. If you ain’t going through nothing, the spirit of God ain’t resting upon you.

“On their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.” Dealing with your families outside the truth: on their part you are being evil spoken of, but on the Most High God’s part you are being glorified with Christ.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer”. We are dealing with a lot of that. Hatred for your brother is a spirit of murder, the spirit of Cain.

“Or as a thief”: people who steal from you, or don’t deal with you wisely when dealing with money; they may as well put a gun in their hand and literally do it, because that’s what they are doing in the spirit.

“Or as an evildoer”: just running your mouth when a lot of times you don’t even know the whole situation. The Bible tells us to prove all things. Don’t just hear one side; hear the whole matter, or next thing you know you’ll find yourself an evildoer, not even realizing it wasn’t what you thought it was.

“Or as a busybody in other men’s matters”: always in somebody’s business, like you ain’t got enough stuff to focus on yourself. We need to tend to our own business. If the Most High wants you to know something, he will make sure you know it. Some of you stay on social media so much that all you do is be a busybody in other people’s matters out in the world, when you should be concerned with what’s going on in the righteous family, helping your brothers and sisters who are struggling and need a word of encouragement, because it’s a fiery trial. What are you doing to build them up? You just want to be nosy and speak bad. You are going to be held accountable for that.

“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed”. You hear the church folks say, I’m a Christian, and they don’t even know what it means. “But let him glorify God on this behalf”: you glorify God by avoiding all this madness.

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God”. First let’s deal with us. Don’t worry about the enemies or the destruction of the enemy yet; first the Most High is dealing with the house of God.

“And if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” Don’t worry about them that don’t obey the gospel of God. Some of them aren’t going to obey God; pray for them and pray the Most High deals with them, but keep being that light and let it shine. People will always be looking for fault in you, looking for you to mess up. None of us is perfect, but we are perfect by keeping these laws, statutes and commandments, and that’s what they don’t understand.

“And if the righteous scarcely be saved”: if we just slide in by the skin of our teeth, that ought to put some fear on you. You know that feeling when you barely got out of a situation, thanking the Lord for mercy, and it stays with you for a while. If we just scarcely make it in, “where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?”

“Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing”: keep the commitment of your souls even through those fiery trials. Sometimes we slip out of the spirit; slide back in there real quick and catch yourself. Do it “as unto a faithful Creator.”

He has been faithful unto us. Through history he has been faithful to the 12 tribes of the children of Israel, even when they cried unto him in the land of Egypt in bondage under Pharaoh, and he is faithful to this very day; that’s how you got where you are now.

We always want to mimic and pattern ourselves after the other nations. Kendrick Lamar, dissing Dre, should have been dissing all the other nations when he said they not like us. They are not like us, because they don’t have the stipulations on them that we have. They don’t have a covenant with the Most High God; we are in covenant with the Most High God. We didn’t know that at one time, because they lied to us and didn’t want us to find it out, but too late.

“For unto us a child is born”: unto who? Unto us. “Unto us a son is given.” Unto us, unto us again.

“And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: not Joe Biden, not Donald Trump. You see they’re trying to take him out again: some fools out here, crazy people who want to be a part of a government like this. They took out our righteous leaders. They took out Christ, one of the most important leaders on the face of this earth and in heaven.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful”: lean back on that, wonderful. Counsellor, “The mighty God”, “The everlasting Father”, “The Prince of Peace.” Man, I can’t wait to experience that peace.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” There ain’t going to be no end, brothers and sisters. “Upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it”: there is going to be some order. That’s why we are trying to get in order now; we are rehearsing the righteous acts now.

“And to establish it with judgment and with justice”: there ain’t no justice and no peace here. There ain’t going to be no justice, no peace here in America, Babylon the great. “From henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

“The Lord sent a word”: what did he do? Sent a word. Sent it where? “Into Jacob.” Ain’t nobody got it like us. They not like us. The other nations don’t have stipulations on them like we have on us; they don’t have a covenant with the Most High God like we have. We are in covenant with the Most High God, and we didn’t know that at one time because they’ve been lying to us. They didn’t want us to find that out, but too late.

“And it hath lighted upon Israel.” They can’t understand why we do what we do. That’s the twelve tribes of the children of Israel right there, over in Oakland, California. I’m proud, and I should be: there ain’t nothing else making me happy in this America, Babylon the great, nothing else to stick my head up and be proud about. You want to be proud to be in America, in the good old USA? You’re fooling yourself; you can get let down tremendously. Look at the black people out there: they proud, they feel like somebody now. Wait a minute, who’s these guys, where did they come from? It’s because the Lord God with his zeal is going to establish this. Look at the woman even with a baby: they ain’t never seen nothing like this. Who wouldn’t want to be a part of this? Look at the girl’s eyes, that old woolly hair on her head: something ain’t right, I ain’t never seen nothing like this, he look like me. They not like us; they want to be like y’all. Look at the elder woman sitting in the chair, raising her hand with what little bit of strength she has, looking in the eyes of the bishop. She’s looking for God, looking for hope, looking for the spirit, and that’s what she’s receiving.

Of the Partridge Family, which traveled on a bus: when the Jackson 5 were one of the baddest groups of that time, the Edomite himself was saying one of the families didn’t even make it off the bus, meaning they didn’t make it in show business because they didn’t have the talent. And in that old clip, one of their lead singers says everybody says you have to be born in the right kind of family, and he’s told that’s ridiculous. No, it’s not; we just read it. This covenant is only unto Jacob. You ain’t born in that family, you ain’t part of that. Then they’re told in this country you can be anything you want to be, and what do they want to be? Negroes. To make it correct, he should have said, I want to be an Israelite. He told him a lie: you can be anything you want to be. Like they say, they not like us. They want to be us, but they can’t be us, brothers and sisters.

Then the woman in the other video saying she loves black women, admires them, wishes she could be black: she love y’all? Yeah, right. She want to be like y’all. She was telling the truth, because we know that down through history. Our men went off to the left, and our women went right off to the left too, but we’re coming back to the right, meaning into righteousness, in right standing with the Most High God. They know this and they see this; the scripture says great fear fell upon them. That’s why we’ve got to get out there so they can see us, so that fear can fall upon them.

You young men, they need to see you repenting, not gang banging, not disrespecting your mothers and your fathers. They need to see you in righteousness, the glory of God upon you as an Israelite, who you are: not no negro, colored, black or African-American. Sisters, they need to see you not out there twerking, running from one man’s bed to the next man’s bed; they need to see you in your glory, glorifying God. Because they not like y’all. The main thing is that we are in covenant: an eternal covenant of life or death, whichever one it is. I hope we all choose life, but we know some won’t. We’ve got to make our calling and election sure, from the … down to the baby that’s in the womb, and think it not strange when these fiery trials come against us.

Esau has to tell you how great we are, but meanwhile our people don’t look at each other like that. Our sisters have the blonde hair, the weave; they’re not loving their own natural hair that God gave them, that looks like him, his attributes. We don’t prefer one another in marriage, we’re not marrying each other, single-parent households. That’s not how God made us.

“And the Lord said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb”: this is Jacob and Esau about to come on the earth, and God separated them. Two nations. “And two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”: two types of people.

“And the one people shall be stronger than the other people.” That was the first clip, the Partridge Family, where they said they wanted to be like the Negroes. It means the Israelites were going to be better than Esau, to the point that they want to take our identity, to be like us, take our heritage, take our culture, cover all the things that we do. But meanwhile our people don’t love each other; they don’t even love them damn selves. We need to come out of that thing.

That’s exactly right: we won’t even love ourselves. God is the author of beauty, and yet we treated like we some baboons, some monkeys or jungle runners. No, we a beautiful people, because God is the author of beauty, and he’s our God.

We are talking about the covenant for eternal life or eternal death, which is damnation. Don’t y’all want to last and exist forever in life? Eternal is without end or beginning: it don’t end, and you can’t even number the beginning of it. That’s how God is. God is eternal; there’s no beginning or ending of him. And there is eternal damnation; it’s not only eternal life. Eternal is essentially unchanging: it’s not going to change. Sometimes we don’t look up these words to get the true clarification; we just say the word and scrape across the surface of it. And God is universal, omnipresent, everywhere. The eyes of the Lord are everywhere beholding the good and the evil. You can’t hide from God.

“For I am the Lord, I change not.” Christianity knows this. “Therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed”: because God made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, that’s why we’re not consumed or destroyed. That’s the reason Jacob ain’t destroyed: God made a covenant with the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. God could have killed us and destroyed us and started over; he was going to start over with Moses.
“Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” Eternal life is what we’re talking about.

“Why callest thou me good?” Man, don’t call me good. “There is none good but one, that is, God”: because he seen us, and he sent us a redeemer, a savior, a sacrifice to shed his blood not only for the Jews but also for Israel, the northern kingdom as well as the southern kingdom. He had to bring Christ on the scene and make him a stumbling block for these Jews called scribes, Sadducees and Pharisees, which we see out here today. You can’t tell them nothing: still out here in the land today in these Christianity churches, these preachers, these politicians. Same people, same spirit.

“But if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” How hard is that?

“Thou shalt do no murder”: thou shalt not hate thy brother in heart, that’s murder. “Thou shalt not commit adultery”: so much foolishness going on in the body in Israel. The Most High is going to deal with you if you don’t repent; thank God for his mercy. “Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness”.

“Honour thy father and thy mother”: young men and young women, hear that. Some of you may not have a father; honor your mother. You’ve got father figures; honor them, they’re trying to guide you in the right path and light.

“Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” We know these scriptures, we bring them out all the time, but we can’t just be hearers of the word; we have to be doers of the word. We are going to be tried on this word to see if we can do it. We can talk it, preach it, teach it, but can we actually put it in action? That’s where the trial comes.
“All these things have I kept from my youth up”: man, done all that since I was a little boy, my grandma says I was a little preacher. All right, you’re going to be tried. “What lack I yet?”

“If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven”. He got hit right here, on thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself; he got cut right here. “And come and follow me”: don’t just do that, but also come and follow me. He was engulfed and tangled up in his possessions, and Christ recognized it: I see you might be a little wealthy, you kept this and that, you’ve got all this.

It’s like here in the world: they confess, I’d like to thank God, I’d like to thank my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. We hear that all the time at these music awards. But let him tell them, go and sell what you have, give to the poor and follow me, and you won’t find one negro running behind him. They ain’t following after Christ, but they claim it: these comedians, athletes, singers, dancers, politicians. It’s a bunch of bamboozling, lying, hoodwinking. When they get tried you’re going to see where they’re at; the cover is going to be pulled off of them.

“But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful”: that thing cut him. “For he had great possessions”: like old Mayweather counting his money at the basketball game, a five-car garage, a home over here, a house on the island, a jet plane over here and another one over there.

What good are your possessions here in captivity, if you can’t help your own people, and you see your people hurting and struggling? You think you did something because you gave out some turkeys at Thanksgiving, or gave out a boatload of shoes to young men who can’t afford those shoes.

Since the Lord changes not, Israel is not consumed. The Lord always redeems his people: from the beginning of the scriptures he always redeemed his people, and he always sent the prophets to wake up his people, as we know from the Book of Malachi that Elijah has come to wake up his people.

“And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people”: he had compassion on the people, so he sent the prophets, the messengers, to give that understanding to his people. “And on his dwelling place”, which is Jerusalem, his people.

“But they mocked the messengers of God”: even now our people still are against God and wicked against the word. “And despised his words”: despised God’s laws. “And misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy”: you couldn’t escape that judgment.

But even though God brings judgment, after the punishment he is still going to bring the word back to his people. He is still going to redeem his people, and that is why the nation of Israel is not consumed.

Think about Elijah running from Jezebel. His life was in danger, but the Most High was feeding him; he sent some birds, ravens, to make sure Elijah was fed. He was in fear for his life, and then the Most High sent the word to him: listen, I’ve got thousands more, don’t worry, I’ve got you. Brothers, don’t worry. Fear is normal, that’s the nature of the flesh, but when you get built up in the spirit you don’t even care no more. There’s still a level of fear, to know to avoid certain things, but know that the Most High God has got your back if you are in righteousness. We make mistakes, we mess up, but if you repent he has your back, sisters too. He declared the end from the beginning. He got us. They not like us; we’ve got a covenant with the Most High God.

“Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel”: we ain’t even seeing that in this day; it’s plenty more. “All the knees which have not bowed unto Baal”: unto idols, unto other gods. That’s why you young men and young women are in a beautiful state right now, a beautiful place: you haven’t bowed your knees to Christmas and birthdays and Thanksgivings and Easter, Valentine’s Day, Memorial Day, the Fourth of July, President’s Day, all this mess they keep rolling around the calendar to keep you in sin, to keep you deterred.

“And every mouth which hath not kissed him”: we’ve got some dirty mouths right here, kissing his ring. That picture of one of them smooching on old Billy Graham, all on that old crinkled-up hand. Man, get out of here; get your mind right.

“I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice”: brothers and sisters, present your bodies, not to fornication, adultery, covetousness, but as a living sacrifice. “Holy”: separated from all this madness in this earth. What is going to help you separate yourself from that is keeping these law, statutes and commandments: ‘keep my commandments and live.’

“Acceptable unto God”: that is the only thing that is acceptable unto God. There ain’t no other thing acceptable unto God but his word. “Which is your reasonable service”: I owe God. If you don’t do nothing else, you owe him that, just for sending the redemption, the Savior for you, Christ the black Messiah. That is our reasonable service, to present our bodies as a living sacrifice. God is going to raise us back up again if we do. So don’t worry about the death: this body has got to die and go back, but the spirit goes back to the Most High God. The one we don’t want to come into is the second death.

For example, the sabbath day and the new moon: we can’t even get brothers to keep them. We understand if you are sick or elderly and can’t travel, but we can’t even get people to keep the sabbath day. We start taking them off the Telegram channels, and we don’t see them until the new moon, to get a cup of strong and a plate full of food, and then they are out of there and we won’t see them for another month. Then they pop up like they’ve been here all year long. It’s ridiculous. You think we don’t watch? We’ve got to do better at watching, at being watchers; that’s why we’ve got ranks, to keep in contact. But we ain’t chasing you no more; that’s the order that’s been put out. You reach out to us, so we can give it not with grief but with gladness: the brother is doing good, the sister is hanging in there, they had to do some traveling, they’ll be back next week. If they’re not feeling good, send somebody over to check on them and see if they need anything.

Next thing you know they’re out there smoking weed, out there jumping up and down on another man’s rod or on some other woman that ain’t their wife or ain’t their husband. You might hide it from us, but you can’t hide it from the Most High God: the eyes of the Lord are everywhere beholding the good and the evil. What God put in every last one of us that keeps us alive is the breath of life, the spirit. If the Most High God takes that spirit out of us, we are just a body. While that spirit is in us, whether you are in the dark and nobody else sees you, the Most High sees you through your own eyes. You are the recorder he sees through, and not only that, he has angels recording. Books were opened: the book of your works and the Book of Life. You can be in a hotel with some woman you ain’t got no business with, and the Most High sees it through the spirit of your own eyes, every detail. Even if he had to put a roach in the corner of the wall, he could look through the eyes of that roach, through the eyes of a bird in a tree. You cannot hide from the Most High God.

There is a spirit in every one of us, the breath of life the Most High put in us to keep us alive. Take that spirit out and we are just a body. And while that spirit is in you, the Most High sees through your own eyes. You are the recorder he sees through. Not only that, he has angels recording, and books are opened: one of your works and the Book of Life. You can be in a hotel with some woman you ain’t got no business with, and the Most High sees it through the spirit of your own eyes. He sees every detail and knows everything you are doing. He could put a roach in the corner of the wall and look through the eyes of that roach, look through the eyes of a bird in a tree. You cannot hide from the Most High God.

That is this scripture. “If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there”, and “if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.” Make your bed in hell and the Most High is there too.

“If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea”: even if you go down in a submarine in the sea, “Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.”

“Surely the darkness shall cover me”: I’m in the room with this woman, I’m hiding, ain’t nobody see me. I snuck off to another town. I’m a truck driver, I’m hitting some stuff. Surely darkness shall cover me. But “even the night shall be light about me.”

“Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee”: the darkness hideth not from the Most High God. “But the night shineth as the day”: in the eyes of the Most High God the night shines just like the day. He sees you plain and clear, in the open, like an x-ray; he sees right through you. “The darkness and the light are both alike to thee”, both alike to the Most High God.

precepts.why:
The Most High putting a roach in the corner is no made-up thing; the Bible says it. “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber”: the Lord said don’t do these things in secret, “for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.”

You can’t hide from the Most High God. You are the best recorder he has. He sees all and he knows all. Your thoughts are not his thoughts, yet he sees your thoughts afar off. His eyes are ten thousand brighter than the sun. He sees it all.

That is how it was when we were little. You did something and mom and daddy weren’t even around, but something in you cringed, like somebody spoke to you: you ain’t got no business doing that, you know better than that, put that back, you stealing, that ain’t yours. That is your conscience, and who gave you that conscience? That is the spirit of God dealing with you. Thank God he dealt with you. At some point we all rebelled, but it caught up with us. How did mama know, how did daddy know? Because the Most High God revealed it.

It is the same with our leadership. They know when we ain’t in the spirit; they see it before you even see it. These are spiritual men, and through their experience over the years their spirit of discernment has increased tremendously. That is where we are trying to get to. You know when your own son or daughter is coming to you with foolishness. You ain’t fooling nobody.

sense.text:
This is the duality: you wanted to do good but you didn’t. Everybody has been through it, knowing you were doing something wrong and doing it anyway, while something told you not to. That is the spirit of God that’s in you to do good. God didn’t create us to be evil, but this flesh makes you be evil, because that is how Satan can manipulate you to do things against the Lord. We all battle with that. That is the test, what the Lord put us here on earth to conquer: that wicked seed.

“For that which I do I allow not”: the I is the spirit within you that God made to be righteous. “For what I would, that do I not”: what I would is the righteous thing I’m supposed to do, that God created me to do, and I do not. “But what I hate, that do I”: the wicked that I don’t want to do, but I end up doing it.

“If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That is what God gave us the laws for: to let us know how to do good. The laws help you stay on that path, that course of doing good and being righteous, because we are susceptible to sin, to doing evil.

Some of these brothers and sisters don’t want to keep these laws, statutes and commandments in the Faith of Christ. They act like they’re in a Christianity church, come when they want to come, like it’s a celebration like Easter. We don’t celebrate Easter; we celebrate the Passover. If you’re sick, we understand; you can’t make it. But try to keep every last one of these high holy days, these sabbaths and feast days. There were times when all I could stay was thirty minutes, but I just wanted to be there, to show the Most High God I’m honoring these laws, statutes and commandments in the Faith of Christ. It is the Faith of Christ that allows you to do that. The sin we’ve done through our lifetime would have destroyed us if God hadn’t given us that grace by sending his son Jesus the Christ, and that goes for the northern kingdom too, which the scribes, Sadducees and Pharisees tried to shut it up from. But God had a plan: he is going to bring us all into the unity of the faith, one spirit and one mind.

“Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together”: we all battle pride within our own spirit. I’ve had to battle my own self. “As the manner of some is.”

“But exhorting one another”: that makes it more important to gather together and get around the men of God, because you may be weak and need some exhorting, some building up. The Most High knows what you need. If I can just get to the new moon, if I can just get to the Sabbath, the Most High is going to speak to somebody through his word to edify you and exhort you. I had to learn that, and I’m still learning it in my times of shortcomings. Separating ourselves puts us in a bad place. The enemy comes in and messes with you, makes you feel like you ain’t a part of nothing. No: you are a part of one of the greatest nations on the face of this earth. It is that flesh you are dealing with. Don’t let it hold you and hinder you.

“And so much the more, as ye see the day approaching”: that day is the day of the Lord’s vengeance. The day of the Lord’s vengeance is approaching. We see it and we understand it now.

precepts.why:
This is why it is so important for us to come together: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” Where your mind is, sometimes it can go off to the left. You need the Most High, and you need to be around your people, so that you are not conformed to this world but transformed by the renewing of your mind, the way you think.

“That ye may prove what is that good”: no, that ain’t good, this is good. I heard it; I saw a brother go through this; oh, he brought that scripture out, I never heard that, this is good. “And acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

sense.text: Just what was said earlier: y’all ain’t hiding it from the Most High God. “The eyes of the Lord are in every place”: every place you are, in the bathroom, his eyes are there. His eyes are everywhere; you can’t hide from the Most High God. “Beholding the evil and the good”: he beholds the evil and the good.
“A city is builded, and set upon a broad field”: it sits in a wide opening. This is the kingdom of heaven, making it into eternal life. And it “is full of all good things”: not some, all good things.

“The entrance thereof is narrow”: it is not easy to get into. “And is set in a dangerous place to fall”: you can literally fall, to the left or to the right. There ain’t no room for error. That is why we have to tighten up.

“Like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water.” You want to be able to walk through that and not fall to the left or the right, because fire can destroy you and burn you, and water can consume you and drown you. Stay in that narrow path and go through these fiery trials. The fire on your right can kill you, but it can also purify you, bring out the true essence and spirit of who you are supposed to be in righteousness in the eyes of Christ. Likewise the water can drown you and destroy you, but at the same time it can wash you and cleanse you: the washing of the water of the word.

So there is good and evil everywhere, and there is a choice, whether you want the good or the evil, with the consequences of the good or the consequences of the evil.

“And one only path between them both”: there ain’t two different paths. You can’t go to the left and you can’t go to the right. There ain’t no detour and no U-turn. We have to go through this, and that is why we have to keep praying for one another. We want to see a lot of our people there, loved ones who have already passed, but that is not up to us, and we can’t judge; some might come in at the very end. All we can do while we are here is our best, keeping these laws and commandments in the Faith of Christ.

“Even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.” I can’t take my wife, my son or my grandbabies. There is only one path, and only one can go there at a time. Work out your own soul’s salvation with fear and trembling. We have to work it out individually.

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance”: it belongs to that man. The inheritance is rightfully ours; that is the Covenant. It is rightfully ours to have, if we want to possess it.

“If he never shall pass the danger set before it”: if he never journeys down that narrow path, how is he ever going to get to that inheritance? How do you get from one state to another if you don’t drive there? It ain’t just going to happen. How are we going to build back the nation of Israel if we don’t go out there and teach the nation of Israel, if we don’t risk our lives? How are we going to bring them back if we don’t journey down that narrow path?

“How shall he receive this inheritance?” We have work to do; it has only just begun. We won’t receive that inheritance if we don’t go through it. I am going to have my trial just like you are going to have yours.

It is going to be a fight. “Enter ye in at the strait gate”: that is the narrow way just spoken of, with water on one side and fire on the other. Your lust, your flesh, is fighting and contrary to your spirit; they are always at war with one another.

“For wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction”: that is why you have to beware. It is easy to fall into sin and easy to do those things, but it is hard to keep the commandments and follow that straight path. We have to keep fighting. “And many there be which go in thereat.”

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.” Stay on that straight path no matter who or what is trying to pull you into that wide gate of destruction. It is going to be a hard walk, but the Most High ain’t tempt us with nothing that we couldn’t do. Keeping the laws is that straight path; the laws keep you going straight. And brothers and sisters are going to help you when you congregate; they will correct you.

“And few there be that find it.” Not everybody is going to find that thing. It is going to be few.

precepts.why:
It is always going to be a fight, and that is why Hebrews 10:25 matters: it is always to your benefit to be around like-minded people. When you start going off, you can talk to a brother or a sister who will help you in the scriptures, someone to confide in who will build you up. When you forsake those things, you are leaning on your own understanding, with only yourself to talk things over with, and yourself is going to lead you to sin: nah, you all right brother, don’t worry about it, just keep on doing what you doing. That is destruction.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit”: it is always a fight. The flesh is trying to keep the spirit down, so you have to feed that spirit. That is why it is good to come on the sabbath days, come to the new moon, come any time we come together, and on these wicked holidays watch the deacons’ classes. A lot of y’all forsake those things and sit at home. Your family calls: why don’t you come through, I know you ain’t doing nothing, get you a plate, we put that good stuff on there. That is the flesh.

“And the Spirit against the flesh”: the spirit is like the brothers calling you, and you look at the phone knowing they want you to come through, but if you don’t answer you ain’t got to say nothing.

“And these are contrary the one to the other”: whichever one you feed more, that is the gate you go in, that is your master, that is where you are going to land. You want to feed the righteous spirit within you more, and to do that you have to be around like-minded people. “So that ye cannot do the things that ye would.”

sense.text:
The straight path is strait commandments. The commandments keep you straight; they keep you in the right path. They won’t let you go off to the left where you fall into the water, and they won’t let you get to the right where you fall off into the fire. Some of you have felt some of that fire and you don’t want that no more; thank God you didn’t fall completely into it. Or you went off and drowned in the deep end, as they say: he went off the deep end, I don’t even know who he is no more, he lost his mind, he’s up in the nut house, running down the street screaming and hollering, cussing everybody out. Don’t fool yourself; you can be there.

“For God hath given strait commandment to such as came, what they should do to live, even as they came”: what they should do to get eternal life, strait commandments. If you don’t want that, you are going to get eternal damnation, eternal death. And what they should do “to avoid punishment”: keep the laws.

“All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme”: thank the Most High God for our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, because every last one of us has blasphemed. You women wearing pants, you are blaspheming. You committing adultery would get the death penalty if it wasn’t for Christ sacrificing himself so that you have grace; you would automatically be put to death. Homosexuality, you can repent from that. Back then, you got caught with somebody else’s wife or husband, you were to be put to death, both of you. You got caught with some sheep, ram or animal, you were put to death and they had to kill the animal too. Thank God for Jesus the Christ.

But if you don’t correct yourself, if you don’t fix this fornication going on in the nation of Israel and all the likeness of sin, if you continue on against the word of God, against the laws of God, you are going to keep blaspheming. “But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation.” You are in danger. We are letting you know it is danger, like the old warning, danger Will Robinson.

Damnation is condemnation to eternal punishment in hell. Ain’t we had enough of this hell we are in now? Haven’t we seen enough happen to our people in this captivity? This is hell. But there is a second death coming. You don’t just die here. That second death is the eternal damnation we are talking about.

precepts.why:
“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” That is why we have to go through that narrow path. They don’t want us to go down that path; they want us to take the broad way. There is going to be persecution and suffering for that, but it is worth it, rather than continue to live like we are living and end up at the very end with eternal damnation.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: everybody in here has ears on the side of the head, but if you have an ear, hear “what the Spirit saith unto the churches”, what this word of God is saying to the churches. Who is the churches? The children of Israel, the twelve tribes. We are the church.

“He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.” We have experienced the first death; we don’t want to experience the second. That is the one. Even this first one, we want to get it right before it takes us out of here, so that we don’t have to experience the second. And you tell me the Most High ain’t showing mercy: he gives you another chance, during the first, to avoid the second death.

sense.text: This is an example of blaspheming the Holy Ghost, of those who are going to fall into that second death. “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened”: once enlightened means you came in here, learned the understanding of the Gospel and started keeping the laws. “And have tasted of the heavenly gift”: we heard about eternal life, the heavenly gifts you get when you keep God’s laws. “And were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”: the Holy Ghost goes to the laws. Made partakers of the Holy Ghost means you started to keep the laws and the feast days.
“And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come”: the kingdom, the power we are going to get, eternal life.

“If they shall fall away”: you go back into the world and fall away from that understanding. “To renew them again unto repentance”: the first verse said it is impossible. It is impossible to renew you again unto repentance. The spirit ain’t going to bring you back; you are not coming back. “Seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh”: that is what you are doing. It is like crucifying the Lord again, just as when Christ was crucified.

We read Revelation 2:10-11, that he that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death; now Revelation 20.

“And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone”. We are trying to bring our people out of the deception, the illusion, the lies. “Where the beast and the false prophet are”: we’ve got these pastors, these scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, the same people that’s here today deceiving our people. That’s a fight we’re up against, not just ourselves. I’m dealing with our salvation first; we ain’t talking about the destruction of them yet, but this is here letting you know that they going to pay.

“And shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever”: did y’all hear that? That’s eternal damnation right there. Day and night for ever and ever; that thing ain’t stopping.

“And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.” You can’t hide from God. You can’t hide in the rocks, you can’t hide under the table, you can’t hide up under the bed; you can’t hide from the Most High God, ain’t no way, no how. Oh, you’re dead? He going to bring you back to life, bring that spirit right back. You can’t hide, so repent; you might as well fix it.

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened”: not the book, but the books. “And another book was opened, which is the book of life”: the Book of Life is what we’re reading out of right now.

“And the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books”. You are being recorded; you’re going to be judged out of that book right there. And there is another book, the things written of the works: “according to their works.” That’s why your whole life is being recorded; all the captivity has been recorded.

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it”: even the sea is going to give up the dead; the Most High is going to call them forth out of the sea. “And death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works”, in righteousness and in evil. Don’t fool yourself: God beholds the good and the evil, and you’re going to be judged from them. That’s why we better repent now. Don’t crucify Christ afresh; repent now and fix it, and don’t go back like a dog to his own vomit.
“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” There it is again: the second death. That’s the one we definitely don’t want to experience.

“And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Lord, have mercy. Out of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, whoever’s name was not written in that Book of Life was cast in the lake of fire.

precepts.why:
Jump over to the next chapter. “He that overcometh shall inherit all things”: he that fed the spirit more than he fed the flesh will overcome. “And I will be his God, and he shall be my son.” You will inherit the kingdom, you will inherit the possession of the other nations, and you will not be destroyed when that day of vengeance and destruction comes forth.

But there’s a flip side to that thing: him that refused to repent, refused to change his mindset, refused to be renewed in the spirit of Christ. “But the fearful, and unbelieving”: you didn’t believe what this Bible said, you didn’t believe that you had to keep the commandments. “And the abominable”: women wearing pants, homosexuality, lesbianism. “And murderers”: ones that hate each other, that want to kill their brothers and kill their sisters, sell drugs. “And whoremongers, and sorcerers”: all those that’s in witchcraft. All of these that didn’t put away this spirit are going to get found in this position, and it ain’t going to be good for you; it’s going to be ugly. “And idolaters, and all liars”: all you that can’t stop lying to save your life.

“Shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”. This is a promise, a guarantee: if you do not want to change and repent, it is promised to you that you will be burned in the lake of fire with fire and brimstone, “which is the second death.” Not talking about this flesh that we’ve got; it’s talking about your spirit, your soul. Some people think, I’ll die and it’s over with. No, it ain’t going to be like that; it’s going to be something nobody ever experienced. If you don’t accept Jesus Christ, if you continue in this sin, we gonna give an account. So let’s make sure we give an accurate and a good account, because if we don’t, it’s going to be manifest, brought forth out of them books.

sense.text:
“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”: all praise to the Most High, Christ is the mediator of the New Testament. “That by means of death”: him dying for the lost sheep of the house of Israel; not for the Jews only, but for the northern kingdom, the nation of Israel also.

“For the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament”: the redemption of the sins we all committed under the Mosaic law, the first testament, the law of sacrifice. Those sacrifices will not help us. They were a schoolmaster, just buying us time until Christ came on the scene to do it once and for all.

“They which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Many are called, but few are chosen. Either you want eternal inheritance, or eternal damnation and death: which one is it?

Little Christianity think they’re saved, sanctified, filled with the Holy Ghost; let me go ahead and kill that now. They think they can go out and sin and do this wickedness and come back; you won’t see them till Easter time, or till somebody died and they up there snotting and crying and asking for forgiveness, oh I’m sorry Mama, all types of foolishness. We see it in the Christianity churches.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: that’s because of Christ. Sin doesn’t have dominion over us anymore through that first testament, the law of sacrifice, because Christ brought the New Testament.

“For ye are not under the law, but under grace”: that law is the sacrificial law; we’re not up under that law. The Most High God got tired of that (you read that in Hebrews 8), because we continued to do the same thing over and over again, and it was not going to fulfill anything for us until Christ came on the scene. Christ is that grace.

“What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.” Those that’s in Christianity: shall we continue to sin because we are not under the law of sacrifice? God forbid you continue in sin, because Christ laid down his life for you once and for all. You don’t continue in sin no more; if they don’t learn it, they’ll see it when that second death comes.

Christianity uses this scripture to say we’re not under the law anymore. But that statement alone tells you: shall we sin because we are not under the law? Sin is the transgression of the law, so it’s a law that is still being kept. It’s not talking about not keeping God’s laws; you keep God’s laws and you try to perfect the law. That’s what grace is about. Exactly.

To that same point. Watch this: Christians really are dumb, but the Bible’s plain. “We then, as workers together with him”: with Christ, “beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” What does it mean to receive the grace of God in vain? Continuing to think that you can sin and it’s okay just because you got grace. The Bible says don’t abuse the grace that we have, because Christ gave us life.

“For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.” Now is the day of salvation, because Christ has come and gave his life.

“Giving no offence in any thing”: meaning we have to keep the commandments. If you’re not offending, that means you’re keeping the commandments; so you can’t abuse the grace, you can’t receive it in vain, as verse one was saying. “That the ministry be not blamed”: that the understanding of the liberty of Christ be not tainted in what it really means.

Just like the Captain said, when we continue to do these things we crucify Christ afresh, killing him all over again. Sin will take you farther than you want to go and keep you longer than you want to stay, and if you get caught out there and don’t get back up under that grace of repentance, you’re in danger of the second death; you’re going to be destroyed. It’s no time to be playing around: the Most High could judge you instantly, driving down the road, walking down the street, walking into a store, falling over dead, a heart attack. You never know when the Most High says, that’s it, I’m tired, cut it off; I’ll see him in the second death. It may be your last chance. This thing is serious, and if you find yourself falling short, fix it as quick as you can: Lord, please forgive me, have mercy on me.

We’re still dealing on the covenant of eternal life or death, the salvation of the saints, and we’re getting ready to get into the destruction of our enemies; we’re going to end off with that. We want to avoid that thing first and foremost; we want to be on the other side watching it go down, not in it.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years”: you young men, you young women, when Moses came to age, to understanding, he “refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”. You ought to be refusing to be called an African-American or a colored or a black. Refuse to be called or associated with Babylon the great; refuse to be called anything outside of a child of God. All the names they put on us, Haitians, Trinidadians, Puerto Ricans, Cubans: we ought to refuse to be called that anymore.

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”: going down that straight and narrow again. He chose not the broad way but the narrow path. If I’m going to suffer, suffer with the people of God, not with the wicked; you don’t want to suffer with the wicked, suffer with your people.

“Than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his soul? When the young man told Christ he had done all these things from his youth, he was told to go and sell what he had, because he had great possessions, and follow him. Y’all see all this entertainment, all this madness that’s going on.

“Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt”: so Moses had faith in Christ; he was knowledgeable of Christ. In Hebrews, what we call the Hall of Faith speaks about Noah, Abraham, Moses, the mighty prophets of God; we need to read that and build our faith. “For he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.”

Moses was come to years. It’s sad to see grown men still out there acting like children; when are they going to come to years? We got to go out there and show them: man, pull your pants up, you grown and still clubbing, chasing women, acting a fool. Women too. What kind of example are you setting for your people? It’s time for us to come to years, not only physically but spiritually. We’ve been behind for a long time, but we got to gain some ground.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” That’s what you see right here: these are the prophets of the nation.

“Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.” We all been a child, we all came through the womb, but we need to come to years and start stepping out on the faith that we say we got. “But the Lord said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.”
“Be not afraid of their faces”: be not afraid, young men. “For I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord.”

“Then the Lord put forth his hand, and touched my mouth.” The Most High had to put forth his hand and touch him, and it’s like he’s touching us: these mighty men out here, who do you think the Most High is touching and putting the spirit on? It is us. “Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth”: not your words, my words.

“See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms”. You don’t realize you’ve been set over the nations and over the kingdoms; through the process of time the Most High has been setting this up already. “To root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” That’s our job, that’s our purpose; this is our profession.

precepts.why:
“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we still have nothing to glory of. This is our profession, what we’re supposed to be doing. “For necessity is laid upon me”: it’s vital that I do this; it is laid upon us. “Yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Woe, destruction, damnation unto me, or eternal life unto me: which one do you choose?

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” A dispensation is a time for you to do what the Most High ordained for you to do, a certain time that this is committed unto us. We got a short amount of time to do what we’re called to do, and if you don’t, it ain’t good.

“But if the watchman see the sword come”: we are the watchmen. “And blow not the trumpet”: Deacon Malachiyah was bringing some of this out during the Feast of Memorial, blowing the trumpets; we are those trumpets. “And the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman’s hand.”

He’s going to require it at our hand. That’s why we have to correct one another and deal with one another in brotherly love and sisterly love. If I don’t, and something happens to you and the judgment falls upon you, then that blood is going to be upon my hand as well as yours.

sense.text:
War is coming to America, Babylon the great; war is coming, brothers and sisters, thus says the Lord, and that’s why we’re here to warn you. Missiles, rockets, all types of destruction: what is a nine millimeter going to do for that, what is gangbanging going to do for that? These countries have such a military that it’s going to take God Almighty to bring them down. Esau is up to his same old tricks, controlling the social media. We talked about the eternal covenant, the eternal death, and the salvation for us that we need to focus on, because the Most High is going to take care of the enemies.

“So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous is what we were just dealing with, trying to get our people in righteousness. Now let’s deal with the destruction of the enemy; we’re going to go out with this one.

Our enemies know it and we know it; we read Deuteronomy 28 all the time. We have been exploited, depleted, degenerated, but we put ourselves in that position. We ain’t going to blame the other nation; we got to take accountability and responsibility for ourselves, and that’s what we’re trying to do now. They’re going to try to stop you and hinder you, so we got to continue to walk that narrow way no matter what, to get into the kingdom.

“Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb”. God says, I formed thee and I knew thee in the belly. Say not, I’m a child; get rid of these excuses, we got a work to do.

“And even to your old age I am he”: even to you old ones, he’s the one. “And even to hoar hairs will I carry you”: he’s going to carry us no matter what. “I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.” Let us encourage you, brothers and sisters.
“To whom will ye liken me”: who are you going to compare to God Almighty? “And make me equal”: who are you going to make equal, the white man, the Arab man? No way.

“They lavish gold out of the bag, and weigh silver in the balance, and hire a goldsmith; and he maketh it a god: they fall down, yea, they worship. They bear him upon the shoulder, they carry him”. What are you doing bearing him upon your shoulder? Are you carrying these gods in your spirit, in your mind? Your head is on top of your shoulders; you’re carrying them right in your head. “Yea, one shall cry unto him, yet can he not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.” He ain’t going to save you.
“Remember this, and shew yourselves men”: bethink yourself and show yourself men. “Bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors”: Lord, we have sinned and come short of your glory.
“Remember the former things of old”: we have done perversely; repent. “For I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me”. There is none like the Most High God.

This is Nebuchadnezzar’s dream. “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”: he’s been setting this up down through history, “which shall never be destroyed”, setting it up so good that it ain’t never going to be destroyed. “And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: it ain’t going to be left to the other people. “But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.”

All these kingdoms and their attributes still exist to this very day in Babylon the great, America, and they influence the whole earth. You had the Assyrian, the Babylonian, the Persian, the Greek, run on down through there.

“Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands”: that’s Christ himself. “And that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay”: the feet are made with iron and brass and clay, and that’s why y’all see so much mess and confusion going on here in America the great. They don’t know if they want to vote for Kamala Harris or Donald Trump, and Biden walks around delirious, don’t know where he’s coming or going. Continue living your life here, thinking this is your eternal life, and see what you get. The clay is over with.

“The silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.” He declared the end from the beginning; the interpretation is sure.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”: that is what we are doing right now, preaching as a witness to all the nations, to the twelve tribes that were scattered.

“And then shall the end come.” So we have a lot of work to do before then. We are just now starting, just now getting a little running in our feet. Be encouraged, brothers and sisters: get your spirit right and repent.

precepts.why:
Drop down to verse 30 and see what comes when the end comes: “then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” He is coming, with power and great glory.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet”: his heavenly angels. We are blowing the trumpet now, the prophets’ trumpet, trying to warn them; but there is going to come a time when the angels sound the trumpets. “And they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” That is the end that follows the gospel of the kingdom being preached as a witness.

sense.text:
They are going to pay for what they have done to the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. “For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you”: he sent us to the nations that spoiled us.

“For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” Whoever touches you touches the apple of God’s eye. You are the apple of God’s eye, you are the only one.

That is vengeance: show these nations something for messing with us. Vengeance is retribution, payback, recompense, exacted for an injury or wrong.

This is set in motion by the angels gathering the elect. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him”: this is why we stand in great boldness, because you afflicted us.

“And made no account of his labours”: you made no account of our suffering, our labours, our trials and our tribulations. But all praises to the Most High God and the faith of Christ.

“The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance.” We are going to see the vengeance, and we are going to rejoice in it too: just like you rejoiced and … as you took us away into captivity, we are going to rejoice to see the vengeance come on your tail.

“He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.” Can you imagine that: washing your feet in the blood of the wicked, and rejoicing about it.
“O Lord God, to whom vengeance belongeth”: vengeance belongs to him. “Shew thyself”: show thyself, O God. We need to pray that, that God show himself.
“Lift up thyself, thou judge of the earth: render a reward to the proud.” The proud are the ones spoken of over and over for their pride: the proud one, the ego.

“Lord, how long shall the wicked, how long shall the wicked triumph?” How long shall they utter and speak hard things against your people, Lord God? “And all the workers of iniquity boast themselves.”

“They break in pieces thy people, O Lord, and afflict thine heritage.” You see what is going on with us, O Lord. If you heard them back then in the time of Egypt, hear us now, O Lord: they afflict your inheritance, O God.

“For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance”: this is what it is coming down to, the day of the Lord’s vengeance. “And the year of recompences”: recompense is payback, baby. The year of recompense and payback, that is what it is coming down to.

It is “for the controversy of Zion,” and Hosea shows what the controversy is.

precepts.why:
This is the controversy of Zion. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land”: in this land called America, Babylon the great, or any of the lands throughout the whole earth. That is the controversy the Most High has.

“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”: we are killing one another, and the Most High has a controversy against that. “Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.”

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”: God is speaking to his people. “Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.” It is time to wake up, brothers and sisters.

sense.text:
“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance.” Praise to the Most High, he is going to take vengeance.

“And I will not meet thee as a man.” It is not going to be an ordinary man like us, with guns and a helmet on, boots, black cargo pants and a purple shirt. It is not going to be the military, with bulletproof vests, tanks, armored vehicles, airplanes and ships on the land, the air and the sea. It is not going to go down like that: he said, I am not going to meet you as a man.
“As for our redeemer, the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel”: the Holy One of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke.” He put on the garments of vengeance for clothing.

“According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, fury to his adversaries, recompence to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompence”: not just here in America, Babylon the great, but even to the islands.

“So shall they fear the name of the Lord from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun.” “When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him”: the enemy is going to come in on us like a flood, but the Most High God is still going to lift up a standard.

“And the Redeemer shall come to Zion”: to where? To Zion. Who is Zion? “And unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob”: we have got to turn from the iniquities of the transgression and bethink ourselves, in Jacob.

“As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the Lord”: this is my covenant. “My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth”: in your mouth, not theirs. “Shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed’s seed, saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.”

From henceforth and for ever: he decreed it, declaring the end from the beginning, from the beginning to the very end, and you are not going to stop this.

“To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God”: the day of vengeance of our God. “To comfort all that mourn.”

Understand this: the Lord of vengeance is going to redeem us, and he is going to fight for us. Never give up, never give in; but for now make sure you work on your soul salvation with fear, for eternal life and not for death.
